newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian PM resumes crisis talks on election rules.
newsitem.headline: Albanian PM resumes crisis talks on election rules.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino resumed crisis talks on Wednesday to try to end a long-running dispute which threatens planned elections.
Italian Prime Minister Romani Prodi, whose country leads a multinational force in Albania protecting humanitarian aid, voiced support for his efforts, saying he expected movement soon.
Fino was working intensively to break a deadlock over disputed electoral rules, which has forced most parties to threaten to boycott the June 29 vote.
Fino held talks all Wednesday morning and into the afternoon and the government was to meet again in the evening.
The parties are unhappy with the current election law, which they say favours President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party.

Politicians said that the government was due to draw up a request for international monitors to take total control of the administration of the election, a move which Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano said would persuade his party to participate in the poll.
"In the afternoon there is a session of the government to approve the necessary request for the international community to guarantee the elections," said Nano.
"We have to wait and I hope for a quick answer," he said.
He said that if the monitors could guarantee the elections would be free and fair, the Socialists would take part in the election under the current election rules.
The elections are regarded as the vital first step in restoring law and order in Albania, still in a state of virtual anarchy after widespread unrest in February and March.
Italian Prime Minister Prodi indicated there was some more optimism after the deadlock of the past days.
"The differences among the parties are very small now," Prodi said during a news conference in Budapest.
"I am confident that we can have some positive steps in the next days or so," Prodi added.
The talks dragged on despite an ultimatum from European envoy Franz Vranitzky, who said he wanted the deadlock solved by the end of Tuesday.

"Time is running out. The government of national reconciliation, the prime minister and the president must reach agreement today," Vranitzky had said in a statement after talks in Vienna on Albania with U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
Italy and Greece have also added their voices to the chorus of warnings from governments.
Albania is still tense after the wave of riots and looting in February and March when thousands of people lost their money in the collapse of crooked pyramid investment schemes.
Vranitzky has made five fruitless mediating trips to Albania since the unrest began and could return this week.
Fino appealed to the West for help to solve the crisis and spoke with Prodi, Vranitzky and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum.
Italy called again for political compromise on Tuesday and Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said the next 24 hours were very important.

Greece said failure to reach an election compromise would jeopardise the continued presence of the 6,000-strong force. Western countries have already warned they may cut aid to Albania unless elections go ahead.
